hypotheses.paper: phi : M -> N a Cauchy extension (N GH singular flat)
hypotheses.note: N T2, connected, second countable carried; phi an IsCauchyEmbedding (DEC-17); phi need not be a structure morphism of the geometry (ett_c_ext_connexe); the Dev form ett_c_ext_connexe_dev is the literal 'Cauchy extension'.

hypotheses.paper: A, B open, containing phi(M), the inclusions phi(M) -> A, phi(M) -> B Cauchy embeddings
hypotheses.note: Read as IsCauchyInclusion (kb/0001, DEC-17; the inclusion is a structure morphism by Geometry.isMor_val). A and B, as spacetimes, need not be connected or second countable, which a Cauchy embedding between singular flat spacetimes would impose.

findings: ETT.tex:1939-1940: the appeal to theo:geroch_sing (M homeomorphic to Sigma x R, to make Sigma connected) is not needed. A ∩ B contains the connected set phi(M), and every point of A ∩ B lies on an inextensible causal curve of A ∩ B meeting phi(Sigma) ⊆ phi(M) (ett_c_ext_connexe_curves, ETT.tex:1941-1942), so A ∩ B is connected for any Cauchy surface Sigma (c_ext_connexe_of_connectedSpace). Suggest: 'every point of A ∩ B is joined inside A ∩ B to the connected set phi(M)'.

ETT.tex:1940-1941: 'the map M -> A ∩ B is a Cauchy embedding, so phi(Sigma) is a Cauchy surface of A ∩ B' is not needed for the conclusion, and it stays unproved even over the geometry. Proved: phi(Sigma) meets every causal curve at most once (ett_c_ext_connexe_curves), and A ∩ B is causally convex in N and globally hyperbolic (ett_c_ext_connexe_convex). The existence half needs an inextensible curve of A ∩ B to lie, through a reparametrisation, on inextensible curves of A and of B. The abstract form (exists_mem_image_inf) is neither proved nor refuted (SubExtensionAbstract SCOPE).

labels.label: prop:Cauchy_pgcd

hypotheses.note: Spacetimes of an abstract CBG Geometry (DEC-60); the E0 instance is owed (T-ett-cbg-e0). Fields used: A1 (rigid), A2 (singularFlatAxioms, curvesExtend, timeFunction) and the structure laws (isMor_*, restrict, isMor_corestrict_iff, absolutelyMinimalOn); no A3/A4, hence none of gx's BTZ obligations. The flat geometry inhabits the hypotheses (flat_cauchy_pgcd).
GH is carried by Dev; connectedness carried ([ConnectedSpace M0], ETT.tex:1502); M0 need not be T2 or second countable.

hypotheses.paper: common sub-extension, its morphisms, maximal, equivalent (ETT.tex:1914-1929)
hypotheses.note: CommonSubDev; its legs are Cauchy embeddings (CommonSubDev.isCauchyEmbedding_b, _c), its morphism notion is ETT's (isMorphism_iff).

The geometry's A1 (DEC-60). Read causally (IsRigid over abstract morphisms), the statement fails for non-local causalities: not_cauchyPgcdAbstract (library's directional Equivalent) and cauchyPgcdAbstract_counterexample_symm (every reading of 'equivalent' that asks for a morphism between the two; the equivalence relation generated by bijective morphisms is not refuted).

findings: ETT.tex:1960-1965: the proof gives more than the statement, and it is proved: the maximal common sub-extension receives a unique morphism from every common sub-extension (ett_cauchy_pgcd), and every maximal one has image the union of ℰ in M1 (ett_cauchy_pgcd_range). Suggest stating it as 'a greatest common sub-extension', which makes 'unique up to equivalence' immediate. The two gaps already recorded for this row are about the paper's text, which still argues neither point: φ is not shown injective (ETT.tex:1953-1960), and the union is not shown Cauchy-included (ETT.tex:1960-1961). Over the geometry both are proved from interface fields: A2 timeFunction (Sbierski Lemma 3.3) gives IsCGHD.injOn, and A2 curvesExtend with causal arc-connectedness gives isCGHD_mcghd. Their E₀ discharge is owed (T-ett-cbg-e0). The recorded paper_findings stay.

ETT.tex:1945-1949, abstract reading (not the paper's setting, DEC-60): the scaffold's abstract statement (CausalScaffold.SubExtension.cauchy_pgcd: abstract 𝕄≥0-morphisms, rigidity as the causal IsRigid) is false for non-local causalities. (a) not_cauchyPgcdAbstract refutes it as formalized. The witness on ℝ has two causalities that agree on every open set of diameter < 1 and are not absolutely minimal (not_absolutelyMinimalOn_witness), and rigidity holds (bigCausality_isRigid). Of two maximal common sub-extensions, bigSub is not Equivalent to the base. The converse DOES hold (base_equivalent_bigSub: a bijective morphism whose inverse is not one). So (a) rests on the library's Equivalent being directional, and under the paper's symmetric 'equivalent' (ETT.tex:1927-1928) those two ARE equivalent. (b) cauchyPgcdAbstract_counterexample_symm refutes it under every reading of 'equivalent' that asks for a morphism between the two: directional, one-step symmetric, isomorphism. In the same setting, two maximal common sub-extensions (ℝ, C', id, id, id) and (ℝ, C'', id, id, id), with C', C'' incomparable between C₀ and C₁, admit no morphism in either direction. (c) NOT refuted: the equivalence relation generated by bijective morphisms. Here i₁ = id is bijective, so the base maps bijectively onto every common sub-extension (via Y.a), and the two witnesses are equivalent through the base (kernel-checked by the AUDIT-2 probe, not stated in the files). Abstractly the one-step symmetric relation is not transitive, and this witness shows it: base ~ C', base ~ C'', C' ≁ C''. So in the abstract setting 'unique up to equivalence' (ETT.tex:1948) needs its reading fixed. Whether the generated reading is refutable is open; it would need i₁ not bijective. Over the geometry all readings coincide (isMor_inv). What this shows: the abstract statement fails without a locality hypothesis, because a carrier's causality is not determined by local isomorphisms. Whether a hypothesis such as absolute minimality (which is not a gluing axiom, kb/0014) suffices is open. It says nothing about the paper's singular flat spacetimes, where the statement holds over the geometry (ett_cauchy_pgcd).

kb_proposals: Non-local relations leave causal curves, inextensibility and Cauchy surfaces unchanged: a causality on ℝ which goes up and contains the timelike line's relations has the timelike line's curves (DensWitness.causalCurveIn_iff_timelike). Non-local relations act only through global hyperbolicity and the strong-morphism conditions. That is how they refute the abstract cauchy_pgcd, where the carriers of sub-extensions may carry different non-local causalities (not_cauchyPgcdAbstract, cauchyPgcdAbstract_counterexample_symm). They give no direct handle on a curve conclusion such as exists_mem_image_inf, whose hypotheses (GH of A and B, φ's IsEMorphism) do depend on them.

The causal IsRigid is satisfiable on a connected, non-trivial base: DensWitness.bigCausality on ℝ (U fills half of ]x,y] in measure, or y - x >= 1) is rigid, because its morphisms preserve midpoints locally. Test any claim that assumes IsRigid against it before trying to prove the claim (T-ett-subextension).

The library's CommonSubExtension.Equivalent (and CommonSubDev.Equivalent) is directional: a bijective morphism X → Y. Abstractly, a bijective IsEMorphism need not have a morphism as inverse (DensWitness.base_equivalent_bigSub). Abstractly, the one-step symmetric relation is not transitive. To refute 'unique up to equivalence', fix the reading first. No morphism either way (cauchyPgcdAbstract_counterexample_symm) refutes every reading that asks for a morphism between the two. It does not refute the equivalence relation generated by bijective morphisms, which holds through the base whenever i₁ is bijective. Over a Geometry all readings coincide (isMor_inv).
